source: Dr. Thaveesak Sangudom, Dr. Theerawut Chutinanthakun, and Wirot Horasart, "Off-season Production Techniques for Pursat Orange (ក្រូចពោធិ៍សាត់ / kroch poursat) in Cambodia," in The Guideline of Climate Change Adaptation in Cambodia (pp. 130-153), Project on Promoting Climate Resilience in Farming Communities of Cambodia, General Department of Agriculture (GDA) Cambodia, Thailand International Cooperation Agency (TICA), and Department of Agriculture (DOA) Thailand, 2017-2020.
text:
Melanose is caused by the fungus Diaporthe citri. Affected leaves develop small dark reddish-gray to black spots; as spotting increases leaves tend to yellow, though this can subside later as the fungus matures into a more dormant state. Fruit affected by melanose develops rough, corky, russeted brownish spotting on the peel.

Control measures given in the source:
1) Prune branch tips and avoid letting the canopy become too dense, so the tree gets good airflow and sunlight penetration.
2) Fungicide spray: copper oxychloride or copper oxide at 40-60 g per 20 L water.
